page: Amazon Web Services i7i.large is a storage-optimized instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 1 physical core providing 2 vCPUs via hyperthreading, alongside 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz. It includes a bundled 468 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed storage operations, with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its Geekbench single-core score of 2290.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 34.55 GB/sec. However, because it is limited to a single physical core, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core are weak. Memory performance is mixed, with average Passmark memory scores but poor uncached large-block read bandwidth of 21.97 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.large provides a dense local NVMe storage allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable entry-level option for storage-bound workloads that do not require highly parallelized processing. It is well-suited for lightweight databases, single-threaded data processing, local caching layers, and development environments requiring fast local disk access.
